clue.text: Seat on a flight, positioned tail-first

indicators.note: the letters are positioned afresh, put into a new order to spell the answer

explanation.surface: An airline passenger has been seated facing backwards on the plane.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Seat on a flight' suggests an aircraft; the flight is a flight of stairs. 'positioned' tells you to rearrange the nine letters of TAIL-FIRST.
explanation.definitionFit: This device is a motorised chair that carries a person up a staircase, literally a seat on a flight of stairs.

clue.text: Drink containing your linctus

indicators.note: the word for drink holds the other piece within it

parts.note: to sup is to drink

explanation.surface: A drink that has your cough medicine mixed into it.
explanation.definitionFit: A linctus is a thick sweet medicine, a kind of medicinal syrup for coughs.

clue.text: Referee arrives to rein in champ

indicators.note: reining in holds something back inside, so one piece goes within the other

parts.note: ARR is the timetable abbreviation for arrives
to champ is to bite or chew noisily

explanation.surface: A match official turns up to restrain an excitable champion.
explanation.walkthrough: 'champ' reads as a champion but is the verb, to chew at the bit.
explanation.definitionFit: An arbiter is someone who settles disputes, the same role as a referee.

clue.text: North Yorkshire town favourite that's walked over by celebrities

parts.note: Redcar is a seaside town on the North Yorkshire coast of England
a pet is a favourite, as in teacher's pet

explanation.surface: A favourite northern town where celebrities like to stroll.
explanation.walkthrough: REDCAR is a seaside town in North Yorkshire, in northern England.
explanation.definitionFit: The carpet laid down for stars at premieres is literally walked over by famous people.

clue.text: Fashionable without function, cape's woolly quality

parts.note: IN means fashionable, as in the in thing
EX is Latin for without or out of, as in ex dividend
to act is to function or operate
a ness is a headland or cape, as in Loch Ness's neighbour Orford Ness

explanation.surface: A fashionable but useless cape is made of woolly material.
explanation.walkthrough: 'woolly' looks like fabric but means vague or imprecise.
explanation.definitionFit: Woolly thinking is vague and imprecise, so a woolly quality is a lack of precision.

clue.text: Piece of driftwood figure

indicators.note: a piece of the word is taken, a run of letters inside it

explanation.surface: A shape seen in a bit of wood washed up on the beach.
explanation.definitionFit: A number written as a numeral is a figure, and this is one of them.

clue.text: Wind giving double trouble at the rear?

parts.note: a twin is a double or exact counterpart

indicators.note: the letter at the rear of the word, its final letter, is taken

explanation.surface: A digestive complaint that causes trouble behind, twice over.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Wind' suggests flatulence, as 'at the rear' hints, but it is the verb to wind or coil.
explanation.definitionFit: To twine is to twist or coil round something, which is to wind.

clue.text: Rough booze's no good after lifting class leader

indicators.note: in a down clue lifting raises the letters so they read from bottom to top
no good means the letter for good is removed

parts.note: rotgut is cheap, harsh liquor

explanation.surface: Cheap liquor is bad news after the head of the class has been drinking it.
explanation.walkthrough: ROTGUT without G gives ROTUT, which 'lifting' turns upward in this down entry.
explanation.definitionFit: A teacher in charge of a small group or class of students is the one leading it.

clue.text: Colourful compounds come from this a Irish way of speaking to an audience

indicators.note: said to an audience means the word is heard rather than read

parts.note: an idiom is a characteristic way of speaking

explanation.surface: Some vivid expression comes from an Irish manner of talking to listeners.
explanation.walkthrough: IDIOM said aloud sounds like IDIUM. 'Colourful compounds' looks like colourful speech, but it is chemistry: this metal was named after Iris, the rainbow, for its vividly coloured salts.
explanation.definitionFit: This element is named from the Greek for rainbow because its salts come in many vivid colours.

clue.text: Morning tea is very English in English ANI Y glasses

indicators.note: one piece goes in, inside the other

parts.note: lenses are the glass pieces of spectacles

explanation.surface: Taking a cup of tea mid-morning is a very English custom.
explanation.walkthrough: VE goes into E + LENSES, after ELE, to give the answer.
explanation.definitionFit: A mid-morning snack and cup of tea is a British custom named after eleven o'clock.

clue.text: Launch with new logo on and off getting withdrawn, say

parts.note: RE means on or about, as in a letter heading
food that has gone off is bad

indicators.note: withdrawn means pulled back, so the letters run the other way

parts.note: EG, for example, is what say means

explanation.surface: A product is launched with a fresh emblem, then pulled back from sale.
explanation.definitionFit: To give a product a new badge or brand name and relaunch it is exactly this marketing move.

clue.text: Do more preparation for painting than big girl's blouse, for example?

definitions.text: Do more preparation for painting than
definitions.meaning: to size a wall is to prime it before painting, so to out-do in sizing
a blouse for a large woman is a garment in a larger than standard fitting

explanation.walkthrough: 'big girl's blouse' is British slang for a feeble man, but here it is literal: a large woman's top.
explanation.definitionFit: Size is a primer for walls, and the word also describes clothes in larger than standard fittings.

clue.text: Bread turned on end

indicators.note: turned means turned round, so the whole run reads backwards

parts.note: at can mean on, as in at the door
a tip is an end, as in the tip of the tongue

explanation.surface: A loaf has been flipped over onto its end.
explanation.definitionFit: A flat, hollow bread from the Middle East, opened to make a pocket, is this kind of loaf.

clue.text: Hoped-for future relief with fat dissolving

indicators.note: dissolving breaks up the letters, so they reform in a new order

explanation.surface: Losing fat brings relief one has long hoped for.
explanation.definitionFit: Life after death is the future many believers hope for.

clue.text: Forester may set out fixed-length tenancy

indicators.note: set out means arranged afresh, so the letters are rearranged

explanation.surface: A forester might lay out the terms of a lease.
explanation.definitionFit: In law, a lease held for a stated number of years is a tenancy of fixed length.

clue.text: It's also not half common

indicators.note: only half of the word is used, its first three letters

parts.note: normal means common or ordinary

explanation.surface: Something that is not even half ordinary.
explanation.definitionFit: This conjunction adds a further negative, meaning and not or also not.

clue.text: Opera diminishes when gloomy note enters

grim means gloomy or dismal

explanation.walkthrough: Britten's opera about a Suffolk fisherman.
explanation.definitionFit: Benjamin Britten's 1945 opera is named after its tragic fisherman protagonist.

clue.text: Doctor who blotted his copybook?

parts.note: a Swiss psychiatrist famous for a personality test built on inkblots, so literally a doctor who made blots

explanation.surface: A physician who made an embarrassing error.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor who' tempts as the TV series; 'blotted his copybook' is an idiom for spoiling one's record, but here read literally as making ink blots.
explanation.definitionFit: Hermann the Swiss psychiatrist devised the inkblot test, so his work was all about blots.

clue.text: It's time warm-up man finished, for the literary audience member

parts.note: to heat is to warm up
Reg is a man's name
o'er is the poetic, literary form of over, meaning finished

explanation.surface: Time is up for the comedian warming up the crowd at a literary event.
explanation.walkthrough: 'warm-up man' suggests the comic who readies an audience, but splits into warm-up and man; O'ER is a poetic contraction of over.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone who regularly attends plays is part of the audience at a performance.

clue.text: Cue intermittently missed in Scouse request for aid

indicators.note: the letters of the first word are missed at intervals, scattered through the second

clue.text: Temporary street work initially going as planned

parts.note: OP, short for opus, is a work

explanation.surface: Roadworks that are temporary are proceeding to plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A stopgap is a temporary substitute, so the word works as an adjective for makeshift.

clue.text: Mean to sequester debt records without respect

parts.note: to imply is to mean or suggest
IOUs are written acknowledgments of debts

explanation.definitionFit: Acting impiously is acting irreverently, with no respect for what is sacred.

clue.text: Waste parts from the heart of buffaloes?

definitions.text: Waste parts from the heart of buffaloes?

parts.words: Waste parts from the heart of buffaloes?
parts.note: the heart and other organs of a slaughtered animal are often treated as discarded leftovers

explanation.surface: Leftover pieces taken from the middle of a herd of buffalo.
explanation.walkthrough: 'from the heart of' looks like a hidden-word signal, but the heart is literal: an internal organ.
explanation.definitionFit: Edible internal organs of butchered animals, like hearts and livers, are traditionally seen as waste parts.

clue.text: Stifling prison

definitions.meaning: stifling means suffocating, causing a feeling of choking
British slang for a jail, from Hindi chauki

clue.text: Simple enjoyment diminished in support for the arts.

parts.note: an easel supports an artist's canvas

indicators.note: diminished means cut short, losing the last letter

parts.note: fun means enjoyment

explanation.walkthrough: 'support for the arts' suggests funding but is a painter's easel; FUN diminished is FU.

clue.text: Mountain animal skinned for pelt

indicators.note: skinning removes the outside, so the first and last letters go

parts.note: the llama is a pack animal of the Andes mountains

explanation.walkthrough: 'pelt' looks like the hide, but it is the verb: to lam is to beat or thrash.

clue.text: A masculine sport without any English mix

indicators.note: every E, the abbreviation for English, is removed

parts.note: male means masculine
a game is a sport

explanation.surface: A macho sport with no English players taking part.

explanation.definitionFit: An amalgam is a blend or combination of different elements.

clue.text: Young man with special quality making a comeback, subject to regular surges

indicators.note: coming back means going in the reverse direction, so the whole run reads backwards

parts.note: a lad is a young man
IT is a special appealing quality, as in having it

explanation.surface: A young man with star quality returns to the stage.
explanation.definitionFit: Waters affected by tides rise and fall in regular surges.

clue.text: See girl come out less quietly, showing bad form

parts.note: a miss is a girl or young woman

explanation.walkthrough: 'bad form' suggests poor manners but means a bad shape.
